Custom Blinds in Los Angeles, California

Blinds give you a simple way to adjust daylight and privacy throughout the day. At John Crawford Company, we'll help you compare materials, finishes and controls, then measure and install the blinds for your windows. Visit our Woodland Hills showroom to get started.

Start with the material and how you'll use it

The room helps narrow the choices. You might want the grain of real wood in a living room, a moisture-resistant material in a bathroom or a vertical treatment that opens easily beside a sliding door.

Think about privacy, how often you open the windows and whether you prefer tilting the slats or raising the blind out of the way. From there, we can compare colors and finishes that work with the rest of the room.

We carry Hunter Douglas and Alta blinds and can help you compare the choices for your windows.

Parkland® Wood BlindsEverWood® Alternative Wood BlindsCustom Metal BlindsAria™ Soft BlindsCustom Vertical BlindsSkyline® Gliding Window PanelsLuminette® Sheer Panels

Parkland® Wood Blinds

Real-wood slats with painted and stained finish choices. We can help you compare the wood tones with your trim, flooring and furniture.

EverWood® Alternative Wood Blinds

A faux wood option designed to resist warping and fading. For a bathroom or sunroom, we can help you compare its moisture and sunlight resistance with real wood.

Custom Metal Blinds

A metal-slat option with a wide selection of colors. Compare the available slat sizes and finishes, with attention to the space needed for mounting and operation.

Aria™ Soft Blinds

Fabric vanes give horizontal blinds a softer appearance and diffuse incoming light. Compare them with wood or metal if you'd like adjustable vanes with a fabric finish.

For wide windows and sliding doors

Custom Vertical Blinds

Vertical vanes provide adjustable light control for wide windows and sliding doors. We'll help you choose the material and decide which opening direction suits the way you use the room.

Skyline® Gliding Window Panels

Wide fabric panels travel along a track and stack to the side. Allowing space for the open panels is especially important at a doorway you use often.

Luminette® Sheer Panels

Vertical fabric vanes within sheer panels give you another way to manage light across large windows and doors. They also appear among the Hunter Douglas sheer-shade and drapery options.

The fit matters when you open the window

Handles, locks, trim and window depth all affect the installation. A blind needs room to tilt, lift or slide without getting in the way of the window or door.

We check those details during professional measuring. Where there are several windows together, we also discuss the layout and how you'd like to operate them. That gives us a clear plan before anything is ordered.

One window is welcome

You don't need a whole-house project to call us. If you're replacing a blind in one room, we'll help you choose for that window and explain the next steps.

For a larger project, we can work through the rooms together and compare where the same material makes sense and where you may want something different.

Questions about blinds

Ask John and Max: (818) 884-5464
What's the difference between wood and faux wood blinds?

Real wood gives you natural grain and stained finish choices. Faux wood offers a wood-style appearance with different material properties, including moisture resistance. We'll help you compare them for the actual room.

Can blinds make a bedroom completely dark?

Closed slats reduce incoming light, but light can still pass through gaps and around the edges. If a darker bedroom is your main goal, we'll discuss suitable shade or drapery options as well.

Can you repair a blind I already own?

We can review the product and available components. Send a photo and describe the problem so we can assess whether repair is possible. Parts availability and the condition of the blind matter, including for products from other brands.
